name: Summoned Companion
description: Conjures a living creature that fights or works alongside its user.

mechanics.text: On activation, a living creature comes into being under the user's control (or friendly to them) for some duration. The specific creature and its own stats live only in this Effect's own notes — too varied to structure generically. Cost tier is keyed to the summoned creature's own challenge rating — used by both spells and items alike, unlike feat.damage's own spell-level ladder, since a summon's real power tracks the creature itself, not the level of whatever conjured it (confirmed live: many summon spells state their own CR ceiling directly, e.g. Conjure Elemental's own 'challenge rating 5 or lower').
A weak or purely-utility summon, challenge rating 0–1 — a familiar, a basic undead servant, a single Tiny animal.
A genuine combatant, challenge rating 2–4 — most Conjure Animals/Woodland Beings-tier summons, a mount, a griffon.

A genuinely dangerous ally, challenge rating 5 or higher — Conjure Elemental/Fey-tier summons, a bound djinni. Also appropriate (regardless of raw CR) for access to a creature TYPE whose own traits matter more than its challenge rating, e.g. a celestial's resistances/healing — GM judgment call, same as any tier.
